criteria.evidence: Turn 0 reply: 'This isn't apt-specific — any job that writes decision entries (apt, snap, flatpak, manual installs) can accumulate the same kind of debris: user uninstalls something by hand... package gets renamed/replaced, a snap revision is purged' with two reconciliation points proposed.
Turn 1: 'No gh CLI, no remote configured, and no GitHub token... Here's the issue content ready to file'; then saved as docs/issues/machine-specific-marks-outlive-item.md at the user's request.

DecisionFile.prune/forget wired into plan() (load-time) and _converge_one plus apt collateral path; row D73 test 'test_a_mark_on_a_collateral_casualty_is_forgotten_once_its_transaction_removes_it' covers the fortunes/fortunes-min case; suite reported passing at turn 4.

The replay's own turn-0/1 proposal (load-time prune, apply-time forget, prune/forget primitives, four managers, INFO logging) is reported implemented at turn 4; doc updates (ADR D-43, PKG-FR-MARK-LIFETIME, coverage rows, runbook) done at turn 5 after user prompt.

Rows H128–H132 and D73 point at tests in package_state (TestLoadTimePruning, TestDecisionFilePrune), package_sync_core (forget on REMOVE) and apt/packages (collateral); per-manager snap/flatpak/manual wiring tests are not visible in the record.

Checks were run only at turn 4 ('pytest 4521 passed... ruff/basedpyright/codespell all clean'); turn 5 then edited five docs including the coverage matrix with duplicate row ids H128–H132 colliding with existing H128–H132, and no re-run of pytest (test_scenario_coverage_matrix.py), codespell or ruff is reported afterward.
Runbook diff adds 'grep -c fortunes ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml  # 0 — the §4 mark did not outlive the collateral removal' and rewrites the prose so pc2's mark on fortunes is gone.

judge.reason: The replay produced a general proposal, an issue file, the implementation and runbook fix, but its final documentation pass introduced duplicate scenario-coverage row ids (H128–H132 already existed) and the repository checks were not re-run after those edits, so c6 is unmet and the replay was turn-capped. Doubt remains about load-time pruning against the manual-only apt inventory and about test coverage of the snap/flatpak/manual wiring, which the truncated diff cannot confirm.
